**Opposite Party No. 2 (Phone Manufacturer/Brand)**

## 3. Facts

1. The Complainant is a consumer within the meaning of Section 2(7) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, having purchased a mobile phone for personal use for a consideration of ₹40,000 in January 2026 (exact date [TO CONFIRM]) from [TO CONFIRM] (seller's name and address).

2. The mobile phone bearing model number [TO CONFIRM] and IMEI number [TO CONFIRM] was covered by a manufacturer's warranty at the time of purchase.

3. On or around [TO CONFIRM], the Complainant noticed a defect/malfunction in the said phone, namely [TO CONFIRM — describe defect], and duly submitted the handset to Opposite Party No. 1 (Service Centre) for repair under warranty.

4. The handset has remained in the custody of Opposite Party No. 1 for approximately three months without being repaired or returned to the Complainant.

5. Opposite Party No. 1 has refused to honour the warranty and has declined to repair or replace the defective phone without lawful justification.

6. Despite repeated follow-ups and requests by the Complainant, the Opposite Parties have failed to resolve the matter, causing the Complainant financial loss and mental agony.

7. The cause of action arose on or around 1 January 2026 and continues to subsist. This complaint is filed well within the limitation period prescribed under Section 69 of the Act.

---

## 4. Deficiency in Service

The Opposite Parties have committed a clear deficiency in service as defined under Section 2(11) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, by:

(a) Retaining the Complainant's mobile phone for approximately three months without effecting any repair;

(b) Wrongfully refusing warranty coverage without providing any valid ground;

(c) Failing to return the handset or offer a replacement or refund;

(d) Causing the Complainant to remain without a functional device, resulting in financial inconvenience and mental distress.

Such conduct also constitutes a violation of the Complainant's consumer rights under Section 2(9) of the Act.

---

## 5. Relief Sought

In view of the foregoing, the Complainant humbly prays that this Hon'ble District Commission may be pleased to direct the Opposite Parties, jointly and severally, to:

(a) Repair the mobile phone free of cost under warranty and return it to the Complainant forthwith; OR, in the alternative, replace it with a new handset of the same or equivalent model; OR refund the purchase price of ₹40,000;

(b) Pay compensation of ₹[TO CONFIRM] for mental agony, harassment, and loss caused to the Complainant;

(c) Pay the costs of this complaint;

(d) Grant such other and further relief as this Hon'ble Commission deems fit and proper in the circumstances of the case.

---

## 6. Sections Relied Upon

| Section | Title | Relevance |
|---|---|---|
| 2(7) | Consumer | Complainant qualifies as a consumer having purchased the phone for personal use |
| 2(9) | Consumer Rights | Complainant's right to redressal and information has been violated |
| 2(11) | Deficiency | Refusal of warranty and retention of handset constitutes deficiency in service |

| 35 | Manner of Filing Complaint | Complaint is filed in the prescribed manner |
| 38 | Procedure on Admission | For issuance of notice to Opposite Parties and hearing |
| 39 | Reliefs | Commission empowered to order repair, replacement, refund and compensation |
| 69 | Limitation Period | Complaint is filed within 2 years of the cause of action |
